verdict.rationale: DeepInfra documents a model catalog on shared, pay-per-token serverless endpoints: you set `model` to a catalog entry, there is no idle GPU time, and it is typically among the first providers to deploy newly released models. However, no evidence names the specific open-weight families in the story, so the breadth and currency of the catalog are unproven. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek and GPT-OSS availability, a documented catalog listing showing its breadth, and independent corroboration of the catalog's currency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can choose among a broad catalog of current open-weight model families (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS and peers) on shared serverless endpoints

citations.quote: DeepInfra is an AI inference cloud that makes it simple to run the latest machine learning models at scale — LLMs, vision, embeddings, image generation, video generation, speech, and more.
Set `model` to a model from our catalog
You only pay per token — no idle GPU time, no minimums, no seat fees.
DeepInfra is typically among the first providers to deploy a newly released model.
Because this is popular model and many people use it, you will not experience the cold-start latency most likely.
